title: Streaming ephemeral token rotation and deletion propagation for analytics pipeline
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The current analytics pipeline has a multi-hour propagation window for deletion requests and PII scrubbing when data is materialized across streaming topics, staged S3 buckets, and downstream analytics stores (ClickHouse/BigQuery). This causes customers to fail contractual retention guarantees and increases legal exposure.

Goal: Implement a streaming-first workflow that enables (1) ephemeral identifiers/tokens for event-level analytics that rotate and can be revoked quickly, (2) low-latency deletion propagation from the control plane to all downstream consumers, and (3) an auditable attestation trail for deletions and scrubs. The system must support legal holds/safe-hold, region-specific retention policies, and backfill-safe scrub operations.

Scope: work touches the console backend controller, streaming gateways (Kafka Connect / CDC layer), transformer processors (Flink/Beam), metadata catalog, deletion-saga, and the audit attestation service. This ticket covers design + implementation of the rotation/revocation protocol, a deletion propagation broker, consumer adapters for ClickHouse/BigQuery/S3, and the monitoring/rollout plan.

Out of scope: full UI for managing retention policies (handled by PM epics), non-analytics ingestion sources (logs pipeline), and on-prem connector implementations (handled separately in Private deployment track).
acceptance_criteria: New ephemeral identifier scheme implemented: short-lived tokens (TTL configurable per-customer/region) issued by console backend and attached to analytics events instead of long-lived user IDs
Revoke API: control-plane endpoint that marks tokens as revoked and produces a deletion event to the deletion-propagation topic within < 10s from API return under normal load
Propagation broker: deletion events are reliably forwarded to downstream adapters with at-least-once guarantees; duplicates are idempotent for consumer adapters

Consumer adapters: ClickHouse, BigQuery, and S3 staging adapters can consume deletion events and perform row-level deletion or safe-redaction within their service-level targets (ClickHouse: < 5 minutes for hot partitions; BigQuery: best-effort streaming deletes and scheduled backfill scrub job)
Safe-hold/Legal hold: deletion requests flagged with legal-hold are recorded and prevented from auto-scrub; attestation records reflect hold state
Audit trail: every deletion/scrub operation produces an attestation log entry with requestor, timestamp, scope, and outcome; attestation exportable via existing audit-export endpoint
Backfill mode: when data is materialized historically, a token-mapping backfill job can reconcile ephemeral tokens to their storage artifacts to support retroactive deletion

Regression tests and load tests: unit and integration tests covering token issuance/rotation/revocation and end-to-end deletion propagation; load test demonstrates propagation latency under 95th percentile target
Operational runbook: monitoring dashboards (latency, failure rate), SLOs defined, and a rollback plan for the deletion-propagation broker
notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PII/Streaming+Ephemeral+Tokens+Design (initial draft, see section 'Broker semantics')
Proto API spec: POST /v1/analytics/tokens/issue, POST /v1/analytics/tokens/revoke, GET /v1/analytics/tokens/status

Decision: favor short-lived tokens + revocation over immediate retroactive row-level encryption changes for performance reasons; we'll rely on deletion events to materialized stores for retroactive scrubs
Trade-offs: at-least-once deletion events are simpler to guarantee in stream relays but require idempotent consumer adapters; exactly-once would add significant complexity to connectors
Privacy review notes: KMS integration required for token materialization keys; encryption-at-rest for ephemeral token mappings mandated by compliance
Related incident: INC-2026-04-high-retention-lag (customer reported 4-hour delay for deletion to appear in analytics dashboard) drove urgency

2026-02-28 - Kofi Agyeman: Prototype for revocation API merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3124 (needs security review before rollout)
2026-03-03 - Security Review (Priya Desai): KMS key policy changes required. Blocker: must add HSM-backed wrapping for token mapping table before production enablement.
2026-03-07 - Data Eng (Lena Zhou): ClickHouse adapter path defined: deletion-events -> control stream -> ingestion micro-batch job -> TTL-mark column update pattern. Performance benchmark attached.
2026-03-09 - PM (Omar Khan): Confirmed compliance requirements for EU customers: max 30-day configurable retention default and regionally-scoped revocation endpoints

2026-03-10 - Kofi Agyeman: Started integration tests for BigQuery adapter; observed edge case where streaming inserts with partition globs require delayed backfill scrub (tracked in sub-issue ENG-56479)
2026-03-10 - Kofi Agyeman: Marking security_review_required=true; raising follow-up to onboarding for Private deployments (ENG-56480)
rollback_plan: Disable token issuance and switch consumer adapters to legacy user-id deletion flow; replay deletion-propagation topic to ensure downstream convergence. Documented steps in runbook and tested in staging.
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards: deletion-propagation latency, revocation API success rate, consumer adapter error queue size. Alert thresholds: propagation latency P95 > 3m OR error rate > 1% -> page on-call. Postmortem template ready.
